title: Strengthening Protections for Lower-income PMEs for Fairer Employment Terms and Working Conditions
what_it_is: Strengthening Protections for Lower-income PMEs for Fairer Employment Terms and Working Conditions

sections.label: PME coverage under Employment Act
sections.summary: PMEs get basic Employment Act protections, but Part 4 protections do not extend to them, and the Ministry is studying support for lower-income PMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Manpower (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Professionals, managers and executives (PMEs) are covered under the Employment Act (EA), which mandates basic protections including annual leave, sick leave and timely payment of salaries.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Manpower (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: However, Part 4 of the EA which provides additional protections to lower-income employees, such as through higher overtime pay rates and limits on working hours, currently does not extend to PMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Manpower (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower and our tripartite partners recognise that PMEs are a key part of our workforce, comprising about 40% of all workers.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Manpower (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Lower-income PMEs may have limited bargaining power and would benefit from additional protections.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Manpower (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: We are actively studying how to strengthen support for lower-income PMEs as part of the ongoing EA review.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Manpower (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: This includes considering how to extend appropriate protections while preserving the flexibility that many PMEs value.

sections.label: Reviewing Part 4 protections for PMEs
sections.summary: Salary levels and bargaining power will be considered in reviewing protections against excessive hours and unpaid overtime, and extending some Part 4 protection is being considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: On his first question, indeed, salary levels and bargaining power are definitely factors that we will consider together with job classification, when we review the statutory protections against excessive working hours and uncompensated overtime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: On his second question, indeed, we are considering extending some Part 4 protection to them as part of the EA review.
